subject: Next steps: Fit validation + risk controls for AcquisitionOps trial
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acquisitionops.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acquisitionops.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap from today's call + priorities

Karthik — thanks for the demo and the thoughtful run-through. A quick recap from our side and the things we care most about: 

- Primary goal: reduce manual QA for acquisition copy by surfacing high-quality headline/CTA suggestions across channels.
- Scale: 5M users monthly, expect ~200k generation calls/day in peak campaign windows.
- Latency target: 300ms 95th for single-turn completions; offline batch reranks can be slower.
- Risk controls: we need deterministic guardrails for hallucination and a repeatable approach for model updates (can't have weekly surprises).

Next steps from our side: share two canonical prompt sets and a representative Eval spreadsheet (we'll attach the examples we mentioned). Can you share recommended model variants, the benchmark you ran for latency/accuracy, and a staging pin option so we can lock outputs during a 30-day pilot? Also need a copy of your SOC 2 addendum and basic MSA redlines to share with legal.

Thanks — Jamie
Director, Product
AcquisitionOps

[Attachment: sample_prompts_acqops.csv (CSV)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acquisitionops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's call + priorities

Jamie — great to meet you and thanks for the clear priorities. High level answers and next steps below.

1) Recommended models and why
- rdx-2-small-qa (quantized): lowest-latency option we recommend for streaming headline generation with strong ROUGE/EM-like proxies in your prompt set.
- rdx-3-medium-tuned: better on nuanced brand voice; higher token cost but fewer post-edits in our tests.
- rdx-3-medium-pin (snapshot): we'll provide a pinned variant for the pilot to prevent upstream updates.

2) Benchmarks we'll share
- latency (p95/p99) across your sample prompts
- generation-quality benchmarks (F1/ROUGE proxies plus manual triage notes)
- cost-per-1k tokens estimates with batching suggestions

3) Risk controls and pinning
- We can snapshot a model version for your pilot (pin) and give you a rollback plan. Pin is scoped to the customer account and kept for the pilot duration.
- We will add a QA gating rule: any model promotion triggers a diff report and a manual approval step for your org.

4) Docs and legal
- I'll share SOC2 addendum and a draft MSA redline; legal will be on copy after we confirm pilot scope.

Next actions — I'll loop in Marissa to send the eval pack and the detailed benchmark artifacts (links + attachments). Expect the eval zip + prompt set within 2 hours. Can we aim to start the pinned pilot next Tuesday (2026-12-14)?

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: request_log_acqops.txt (internal note)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acquisitionops.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T18:20:00-08:00
Subject: Eval pack + benchmark links for AcquisitionOps pilot

Hi Jamie / team — attaching the eval pack and a short guide to reproduce the benchmarks we ran. Key callouts below so things are easy to review: 

- What we ran: 3k representative prompts (you provided 150; we synthetically varied length/temperature) and a rule-based set for hallucination detection.
- Recommended starting variant: rdx-3-medium-pin (the snapshot we prepared) — balances brand fidelity and acceptable latency.
- Tradeoffs: rdx-2-small-qa hits your latency target easily but underperforms on identity retention for longer prompts; we included side-by-side diffs in the report.

Important: We observed small output deltas between rdx-3-medium at v20261122 and v20261202 (mixed in the wild) on roughly 7% of prompts where brand tone changed. That’s the kind of regression we want to avoid mid-pilot. For that reason we recommend: 
  - Pilot starts on the pinned snapshot (rdx-3-medium-pin) provided below.
  - If you later want an upgrade, we'll run a gated promotion: automated diff + your canonical prompt suite run, then a 48-hour canary with your traffic if acceptable.

Attachments (in this email): acqops_eval_pack_v1.zip (includes prompts, eval harness, and instructions); acqops_prompt_set_v1.csv; acqops_benchmark_report_v20261209.pdf

Links: 
- Evaluation folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/acqops-eval-4783
- Benchmark dashboard (read-only): https://redwood.ai/bench/acqops/DEAL-4783

If you want, Aditya can kick off a short live session to walk through the diff tool and how pinning works from an operational perspective.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: acqops_eval_pack_v1.zip (archive)]

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acquisitionops.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acquisitionops.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-10T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval pack + benchmark links for AcquisitionOps pilot

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Marissa. A couple of clarifying items from our side: 

- Pilot scope: we'd like to start with a subset (three high-volume campaigns) to validate latency and brand fidelity under load.
- Pinning: we absolutely need the snapshot for the pilot window. Please confirm SLA around pinned snapshots (e.g., security patches yes, model weight changes no) and how long you will keep the snapshot available after the pilot.
- Regression alerts: can you push a baseline diff report into our Slack channel (we'll provide an integration token) and also include a summary CSV with the 7% diffs you mentioned?
- Legal: our GC wants the MSA redlines and SOC 2 addendum; can you send those to my legal contact (elena.garcia@acquisitionops.com)?

If you can confirm the above by EOD PST we'll prepare the internal sign-off for a Tuesday start.

Tom
VP Growth, AcquisitionOps

[Quoted text below]
On Thu, Dec 9, 2026 at 6:20 PM marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Jamie / team — attaching the eval pack and a short guide to reproduce the benchmarks we ran....

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acquisitionops.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-10T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval pack + benchmark links for AcquisitionOps pilot

Tom — quick confirmations and operational notes: 

1) Pinned snapshot SLA
- Security patches (control-plane and infra) applied as needed; pinned model weights are immutable for the duration of the pilot unless you request a promotion. 
- Snapshot retention: we keep pinned snapshots for 90 days after pilot end by default; extended retention available if requested.

2) Regression/diff reporting
- We'll push an automated diff CSV into the Slack channel and the Drive folder after each gated promotion attempt. The diff CSV includes per-prompt tokens changed, edit distance, and a simple "regression_score" column.
- For the 7% diffs: that's a conservative overall figure from our test suite; the benchmark_report contains the specific examples.

3) Legal docs
- MSA redlines and SOC 2 addendum: sending to elena.garcia@acquisitionops.com now (cc'd to Karthik). Expect separate email with DocuSign link for signature where applicable.

4) Next Ops step
- Karthik: we'll provision the pinned snapshot (rdx-3-medium-pin) in your test namespace and grant AcquisitionOps a read-only link to the benchmark dashboard.
- Marissa / Neha: please coordinate the canary run schedule and Slack integration for diff push.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign link and the initial provision confirmation shortly.

Best,
Aditya Rao
SRE/Operations, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: msa_draft_acqops.docx (document)]
